title: Supported Python runtime
requirement: The package shall declare and test one supported Python runtime range and reject unsupported interpreters before normal execution.
rationale: A clear runtime contract prevents unsupported installations and false compatibility claims.
verification: Build and install release artifacts on every declared Python version; run help, version, initialization, and core lifecycle smoke tests.

title: Canonical files and rebuildable projections
requirement: Core Roadmap entities shall have one human-readable versioned Markdown and YAML representation at the stable ID-based path defined by ADR-0010; databases indexes caches and analytics views shall be disposable projections.
rationale: Diffable portable canonical storage is the central product constraint while projections provide scalable queries.
verification: Round-trip representative entities and relations; delete corrupt and stale every projection; rebuild from files; compare semantic queries; verify canonical files always win disagreements.

title: Enforced architecture boundaries
requirement: Production modules shall follow the documented inward dependency direction enforced by stock Import Linter contracts and narrow namespace/core guards with no migration exceptions.
rationale: Enforced boundaries limit coupling and turn the migration into a ratchet.
verification: Run valid and forbidden-import fixtures including layer cycles relative imports aliases TYPE_CHECKING missing dependencies and retired namespaces; verify nonzero failure exits and rejection of any nonempty baseline.

title: Stable CLI contract
requirement: Documented commands options exit-code categories and machine-readable output shall remain compatible within a release line unless a breaking change is approved and documented; incidental human presentation and internal Python imports are not public by default.
rationale: Users and scripts depend on predictable declared behavior while internal architecture must remain evolvable.
verification: Exercise documented commands through installed-artifact tests; snapshot command schemas and structured output; require migration notes for approved breaks.

title: Owned validation and typed failures
requirement: Adapters shall validate representation Domain shall enforce single-aggregate invariants Application shall enforce contextual and cross-aggregate rules and inbound adapters shall translate typed failures to stable user-facing behavior.
rationale: One owner per rule prevents duplicated policy and framework leakage.
verification: Test valid boundary and invalid CLI configuration frontmatter CSV identifier date enum aggregate and cross-aggregate cases; assert failure category cause redaction exit behavior and no mutation.

title: Credential exclusion and redaction
requirement: Roadmap shall not store Git or provider credentials and shall not serialize sensitive runtime values into repository data exported output telemetry or logs.
rationale: Repository data is commonly committed and shared.
verification: Test legacy credential removal runtime redaction log capture export error behavior and absence of credential keys or persistence on supported platforms.

title: Safe filesystem scope
requirement: All user-influenced paths and filenames shall be normalized, validated, and constrained to the intended project scope before file operations.
rationale: The CLI must prevent traversal, symlink escape, and unintended overwrite or deletion.
verification: Test traversal, symlink, invalid name, overwrite, permission, temporary-file, and archive edge cases; run the high-severity Bandit gate in CI and use targeted Semgrep reviews for security-sensitive changes.

title: Atomic and recoverable mutations
requirement: Every mutating use case shall run in an Application-owned unit of work implemented with workspace concurrency control atomic same-filesystem replacement conflict detection and deterministic recovery of interrupted multi-document commits.
rationale: Partial writes and concurrent edits can corrupt canonical project data.
verification: Inject interruption after every stage and test concurrent writers external edits disk-full permission loss stale locks rollback or roll-forward and projection failure on every supported OS.

title: Offline core operation
requirement: Core entity configuration reporting health recovery and repository-inspection operations shall not require network access or a provider client.
rationale: Offline-first behavior is a product promise and Git owns repository transport.
verification: Run core journey tests with network access blocked; verify no Roadmap operation performs hidden fetch pull push or remote entity reconciliation.

title: Boundary failure isolation
requirement: Filesystem local Git telemetry database and external-command failures shall be translated by their adapters into bounded typed failures without corrupting canonical Roadmap data.
rationale: External mechanisms fail independently of local planning rules.
verification: Inject timeout permission malformed output stale data cancellation and process failures; verify typed causal errors redaction canonical readability and deterministic recovery.

title: Automated quality gate
requirement: Every code change shall pass formatting, linting, type, architecture, security, complexity, dead-code, package, documentation, and automated test gates defined in CI.
rationale: A visible failing gate keeps the repository maintainable and reviewable.
verification: Use negative gate tests to prove each policy fails when violated and verify required jobs complete on pull requests.

title: Cross-platform behavior
requirement: Supported CLI behavior and canonical data shall be portable across every declared operating system without platform-specific import or path failures.
rationale: The project targets developer workstations and repository portability.
verification: Run artifact and journey tests on the full OS matrix; include path, lock, newline, encoding, shell, and executable discovery cases.

title: Deterministic structured output
requirement: JSON, CSV, and other machine-readable output shall be syntactically valid, deterministic for equivalent inputs, schema-versioned where persisted, and separated from diagnostics.
rationale: Reliable output enables shell pipelines, reporting, and interchange.
verification: Parse emitted formats; validate documented schemas; compare equivalent inputs; test nulls, Unicode, delimiters, errors, empty data, and stdout/stderr separation.

title: Structured observability
requirement: Logs audit events and optional telemetry shall provide correlation and diagnostic context without secrets changes to command results or a second store for canonical history.
rationale: Actionable diagnostics shorten recovery while Git history remains the audit source for committed roadmap state.
verification: Capture representative success failure retry and recovery diagnostics; verify severity correlation redaction disabled mode output isolation and no duplication of canonical content.

title: Documentation and release traceability
requirement: User-visible behavior changes shall update relevant documentation, requirements, migration guidance, and the Unreleased changelog.
rationale: Traceability keeps product claims, implementation, and release communication aligned.
verification: Review pull requests for requirement IDs, acceptance evidence, docs, changelog, migrations, and passing link/build checks.

title: Isolated distributable package
requirement: Release artifacts shall contain the Roadmap package and console entry point without runtime dependencies that shadow its import namespace.
rationale: The primary user journey begins with a working installed command.
verification: Build wheel and sdist in a clean job; inspect metadata; install each artifact without the source tree; run help, version, and import smoke tests.

title: Consistent command execution
requirement: Every command shall use common context discovery, error translation, confirmation, dry-run, and exit-code conventions.
rationale: Consistent mechanics make a broad CLI learnable and scriptable.
verification: Run contract tests across representative read, write, destructive, local-Git, and repair commands; assert output channel and exit behavior.

title: Idempotent workspace initialization
requirement: Workspace discovery and initialization shall be idempotent and dry-runnable, preserve existing canonical data, and reject invalid configuration before creating a destination.
rationale: Initialization errors must not destroy the first user experience or prior project data.
verification: Test clean existing partial custom-name explicit-workspace invalid configuration and interrupted initialization; deprecated force interactive and template flags warn without authorizing overwrite or changing the supported plan.

title: Scoped versioned configuration
requirement: Every configuration key shall declare project user or invocation scope and use a validated versioned schema with explicit defaults typed Bootstrap resolution scoped reset and forward migration; credentials machine paths and Git policy shall not be stored as shared project configuration.
rationale: Configuration drift and ambient access affect every journey and can expose sensitive values.
verification: Round-trip every scope; reject invalid cross-scope values; test allowed overrides immutable injection resets migrations redaction and absence of Git or sync credentials in Roadmap configuration.

title: Stable identity and referential integrity
requirement: Every aggregate shall have a stable opaque Roadmap ID and every typed relationship shall persist the complete ID and validate across visible closed archived indexed and externally referenced state; existing IDs remain unchanged and new IDs use UUID4.
rationale: Traceability and safe recovery depend on identity that is independent of names paths and providers.
verification: Test legacy and UUID4 IDs collisions ambiguous CLI prefixes rename reassignment close archive restore external references missing targets duplicate links stale indexes and cross-aggregate lookups.

title: Valid workflow and retention transitions
requirement: Workflow status and retention lifecycle shall be separate explicit state machines with validated transitions reasons timestamps and idempotent behavior; archive shall not replace workflow status or change canonical path.
rationale: Conflating completion retention and storage location corrupts history and query meaning.
verification: Exhaustively test permitted and rejected close reopen archive restore and purge transitions repeated events derived progress visibility stable paths and relationship resolution.

title: Validated dependency graphs
requirement: Dependency relations shall prevent missing targets self-links duplicates and prohibited cycles and shall expose deterministic traversal and critical-path analysis across every retained lifecycle state.
rationale: Invalid graphs make scheduling and execution unreliable.
verification: Use property and example tests for graph mutation cycles disconnected nodes archived targets critical paths and large graphs.

title: Durable comments and lifecycle history
requirement: Issue comments and lifecycle events shall retain stable authorship timestamps targets ordering and history while committed canonical content remains inspectable through Git.
rationale: Context and accountability must survive handoff repository history and archive transitions.
verification: Round-trip comment creation reply listing close archive restore purge corruption and migration cases; verify authorship ordering stable targets and Git-visible canonical diffs.

title: Derived planning aggregates
requirement: Project milestone board and daily views shall derive counts and progress from canonical linked entities using one documented Application-owned calculation policy.
rationale: Duplicated or stale progress erodes planning trust.
verification: Reconcile aggregates after create reassignment transition archive restore projection rebuild and manual file edit; test empty overdue partial and stale-index states.

title: Safe Git command boundary
requirement: Git operations shall use bounded argument arrays, explicit repository scope, timeouts, cancellation, and translated errors without shell injection.
rationale: Git is both a core integration and an external failure boundary.
verification: Test dirty trees, missing Git, nested repositories, unusual paths, timeouts, command failure, branch collisions, and cancellation.

title: Reversible Git-hook integration
requirement: Roadmap-managed Git hooks shall be idempotent, composable with existing hooks, identifiable, configurable, and removable without deleting user content.
rationale: Hook installation modifies developer workflows and must be reversible.
verification: Test install/status/config/uninstall with absent, existing, chained, damaged, and repeated hook states on supported platforms.

title: Deterministic commit reference parsing
requirement: Commit parsing shall recognize only documented unambiguous references and apply idempotent mapped transitions.
rationale: False positives can change work state from ordinary commit prose.
verification: Use a table of valid, invalid, ambiguous, repeated, Unicode, multiline, revert, merge, and unknown-ID messages.

title: Git-owned synchronization boundary
requirement: Roadmap shall treat canonical repository files as its only synchronized state and shall not implement provider backends baselines three-way entity reconciliation or implicit fetch pull merge rebase or push operations.
rationale: One synchronization authority avoids a second distributed-state protocol.
verification: Run collaboration journeys with standard Git and blocked application network access; assert no Roadmap sync configuration checkpoint remote mapping or hidden transport is required.

title: Rebuildable derived projections
requirement: Every database index cache analytics table and materialized view shall be derivable from canonical files detect stale or incompatible state and rebuild idempotently without changing canonical content.
rationale: Query performance must not create a competing source of truth.
verification: Delete corrupt truncate age and schema-mismatch every projection; rebuild repeatedly; compare query results and canonical file digests before and after.

title: Stable lifecycle storage
requirement: Canonical entity paths shall use the flat collection and complete-ID layout from ADR-0010 and shall not change when title membership workflow status or archive visibility changes.
rationale: Mutable business state must not be encoded as a storage address or query index.
verification: Test legacy-layout migration rename reassignment close reopen archive restore and projection rebuild; assert one stable canonical path no duplicates Git-visible content-only changes and retained ID lookup.

title: Explicit external references
requirement: External URLs and identifiers shall be ordinary optional references that never replace Roadmap identity trigger network access or create baseline mapping and reconciliation state.
rationale: External context can be useful without introducing a second writable source.
verification: Round-trip add edit remove missing malformed duplicate and archived-reference cases; assert stable Roadmap identity no network calls and no provider-specific domain dependency.

title: Versioned export and report schemas
requirement: Export and report formats shall have documented fields, stable identifiers, deterministic ordering, safe overwrite behavior, and schema versions where compatibility requires them.
rationale: Exports become downstream interfaces and backup inputs.
verification: Golden-file and parser tests shall cover filters, Unicode, nulls, empty sets, quoting, column selection, schema changes, and file collisions.

title: Safe diagnostics and repair
requirement: Health, integrity, cleanup, and repair operations shall separate detection from mutation and provide exact findings, stable severity, dry-run, confirmation, recovery, and post-check evidence.
rationale: Automated repair is destructive unless its scope and result are auditable.
verification: Test each detector/fixer pair with healthy, damaged, ambiguous, permission-denied, partial-failure, dry-run, and repeated execution cases.

title: Backup, lifecycle, and recovery integrity
requirement: Backup archive restore purge and transaction-recovery operations shall preserve stable identity path relationships metadata and recoverability through atomic scoped changes.
rationale: Recovery features must be more trustworthy than the failure they address.
verification: Run deterministic round-trip and failure-injection tests for all entities nested relations collisions interrupted commits visibility transitions retention purge manual edits and post-recovery health checks.

title: Versioned data migration
requirement: Every canonical schema shall declare a version and provide explicit idempotent forward migration with preflight recovery guidance and unsupported-future-version rejection; projection schemas shall be rebuildable instead of migrated as authority.
rationale: Long-lived repository data outlives individual CLI releases.
verification: Test each supported source version repeated migration partial failure future-version rejection preserved legacy IDs UUID4 creation stable target paths archived metadata duplicate conflicts unknown-field preservation projection rebuild and semantic round-trip.

title: Measured performance envelope
requirement: Interactive and batch journeys shall have documented dataset-size and latency targets and shall avoid unbounded memory filesystem parsing and Git work; normal filtered queries shall use rebuildable projections where measurement justifies them.
rationale: Large retained and archived histories must remain predictable for the stated small-team audience.
verification: Benchmark list lookup daily board health dependency projection rebuild and export journeys at defined visible closed and archived entity counts; fail on material regressions.

title: Requirement artifact schema
requirement: User and technical requirements shall use a shared versioned canonical envelope with UUID identity, readable key, type-specific criteria, lifecycle, ownership, content revision and timestamps.
rationale: A small coherent schema enables governance without heavyweight tooling.
verification: Validate minimal/complete/invalid/unknown-field documents; preserve body/frontmatter through round trips; detect duplicate UUIDs and readable keys; no evidence is required to create a Draft.

title: Requirement repository
requirement: Explicit requirement use cases shall create, load, update and query canonical requirements through Application-owned ports and the existing transaction/recovery boundary.
rationale: Requirements need the same file-first guarantees as other core entities.
verification: Test same-filesystem writes, manual edits, conflict refusal, unknown-field/body preservation, read-only lookup and projection rebuild on supported systems. CSV interchange, requirement archive commands and supersession remain deferred.

title: Governed requirement lifecycle
requirement: Requirement status transitions shall be explicit, validated and attributed; governed approval/verification shall never be inferred solely from linked work state.
rationale: Requirements are decisions, not task status aliases.
verification: Exercise every accepted transition and refusal, reacceptance after semantic edits, reasons/actor/time, deferred/rejected eligibility and separation of derived progress from governed status. Actor metadata is not an authorization service.

title: Typed traceability graph
requirement: Typed requirement relations shall have one defined canonical owner, UUID targets and derived reverse discovery, with target-type, duplicate, missing-target and cycle validation.
rationale: Typed traceability separates intent, implementation, planning, and evidence.
verification: Test supports/depends-on/implemented-by/project-target/milestone-target/evidence/report links, reverse lookup, unlinking, closed/archived targets, manual broken references and concurrent/failing writes. Supersession and generic graph plugins remain deferred.

title: Transactional requirement CSV interchange
requirement: Requirement CSV export and import shall be deterministic, round-trip supported fields, validate the whole change set, preview conflicts, and commit atomically.
rationale: CSV is useful for bulk review but must not become a divergent source of truth.
verification: Export canonical fixtures, re-import unchanged and modified copies, inject invalid and conflicting rows, and verify dry-run and rollback behavior.

title: Traceability and coverage queries
requirement: Coverage calculations shall use explicit eligible populations and relations and shall expose missing work, evidence, dependencies, and orphan implementation by journey, priority, milestone, and release.
rationale: Coverage must reveal gaps rather than reward record count.
verification: Reconcile terminal and versioned JSON classifications to explicit eligible populations for empty/partial/complete/archived/broken graphs; cover planned, implemented, awaiting/stale/failed verification, maintenance justification and deterministic order without fabricated links.

title: Verification evidence and audit
requirement: Requirement verification records shall identify criterion coverage, result, stable location, applicable content revision/commit/artifact, attributed reviewer and time, and preserve stale evidence after edits.
rationale: A Verified label without evidence provides false assurance.
verification: Test missing/partial/passing/failing/stale evidence, acceptance-bearing content changes and non-semantic metadata edits; refuse verification without current passing coverage; retain earlier evidence; do not execute arbitrary evidence references or treat file existence as proof.

title: Requirement schema migration
requirement: Requirement artifacts and relations shall participate in versioned workspace migration without losing stable IDs, history, evidence, or supersession links.
rationale: Requirements are intended to outlive implementation work and releases.
verification: Migrate every supported requirement schema fixture, repeat migrations, interrupt and resume, reject future schemas, and compare semantic graphs before and after.

title: Requirements domain architecture fit
requirement: Before requirement entities are implemented, the planned Domain, Application, and Adapter packages for requirements shall be checked against the existing hexagonal zones in architecture.toml and shall not require a new zone, phase bump, or exception; if they do not fit, an ADR amendment shall be written first.
rationale: Adding a new entity family after Phase 13 must not silently reopen the architecture ratchet or bypass enforced dependency direction.
verification: Map the proposed requirements package layout onto architecture.toml zones and rules; run the architecture policy test against a draft fixture before real implementation begins; document the fit or the required ADR amendment.

title: Git-hosting link generation
requirement: Roadmap shall detect the hosting provider (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, or unrecognized) from the local Git remote and generate correctly shaped issue, branch, and pull/merge-request URLs through a distinct read-only hosting URL command (recommended `roadmap git url`, pending CLI contract review) using only local repository data, with no network calls and no stored credentials.
rationale: Contributors want a ready-to-use link without Roadmap acting as a provider client or holding remote credentials.
verification: Test recognized and unrecognized remote URL shapes (HTTPS and SSH), multiple remotes, missing remotes, and malformed remote configuration; assert no outbound network call and no credential storage. Preserve the current mutating git link contract unless explicitly migrated.

title: Gantt and critical-path visualization
requirement: Schedule presentation shall use one Application-owned calculation, provide terminal and versioned JSON output and select rendering after comparing two approaches without compromising isolated packaging.
rationale: Visualizing sequence and slack makes the existing critical-path calculation actionable instead of just numeric output.
verification: Compare terminal/Unicode versus standalone static export before selecting optional exports; assert schedule/slack/critical-path consistency for branching/equal-length/empty/large graphs, missing estimates and cross-scope dependencies; no calendar/capacity claims beyond the declared model.

title: Requirement identity and readable keys
requirement: Requirement identity shall follow UUID4 and flat canonical-path ADRs while readable UR/TR keys are separate workspace-unique aliases.
rationale: Branch-independent allocation must never silently duplicate or rebind identity.
verification: Test local allocation under lock, concurrent-branch alias collisions, explicit collision resolution preserving UUIDs/links/history, case-stable paths and unambiguous lookup. Final alias allocation/resolution interface is an implementation design gate.

title: Acceptance revision and stale verification
requirement: Requirement acceptance-bearing content shall have an explicit revision/fingerprint to which verification applies; changes preserve history and invalidate current verification.
rationale: Evidence must not silently certify changed intent.
verification: Exercise statement/criteria/scope changes, metadata/format-only changes, valid manual edits, conflict/retry and prior-evidence retention; a selected canonicalization policy is tested before implementation.

title: Deterministic next-work policy
requirement: Next-work queries shall apply explicit eligibility, ordering, stable tie-breaking and explanation policies with an injected planning time and no canonical mutation.
rationale: Recommendations should expose product choices rather than hide them in a score.
verification: Reconcile examples for urgent defects, milestone commitments, deadlines, unmet dependencies, unblocking value, missing estimates, maintenance and ready-to-verify work; policy weights/order require maintainer decision before implementation.

title: Optional requirements adoption contract
requirement: Requirements support shall be additive and optional, participate in explicit versioned migration where needed and preserve supported issue-only workflows.
rationale: Requirements must not impose ceremony or hidden writes on existing users.
verification: Installed 0.3.1 fixture journeys before/after adoption; absent requirements collection, migration preview/failure/retry, supported future-version rejection and documented downgrade boundary; canonical reads never introduce files.

title: Self-hosted development evidence
requirement: Roadmap release work and dogfooding observations shall be captured through the installed CLI in version-controlled canonical work items, with reproducible release-review evidence.
rationale: Real workflow friction is development input rather than an anecdote or coverage statistic.
verification: Audit work-item links, installed version, observations and dispositions; candidate tests use copies; retain historical workspace IDs and migration evidence; verify one authoritative requirements-store cutover and a self-hosted release journey.

title: Explicit external backlog disposition
requirement: Baseline GitHub reports shall map to local work items by repository-qualified URL; remote disposition shall be a separate explicit gh action with auditable retry and state verification.
rationale: Local and GitHub writes cannot form one atomic transaction or imply provider synchronization.
verification: Verify baseline completeness/uniqueness, reconciliation of existing IDs, exact repository/number identity, completed versus not-planned rationale, failed remote actions and final remote-state audit. Preserve closure evidence locally; no automatic sync or local-done-equals-remote-closed assumption.

title: Dependency schedule semantics
requirement: One Application-owned dependency schedule shall calculate earliest/latest starts and finishes, all critical paths and slack under explicit unlimited-parallelism and planning-time assumptions.
rationale: Longest path alone is not a complete schedule or resource forecast.
verification: Test fork/join/equal critical paths, dependency cycles, outside-scope predecessors, absent estimates, explicit defaults, UTC continuous-hour planning, deadlines and deterministic tie ordering; no silent four-hour fallback or assignee-capacity forecast.

title: Two-clone completion correctness
requirement: Git-authored canonical completion shall be visible on the first relevant read after pull through projection freshness handling without additional canonical mutations.
rationale: Git collaboration must carry completed work, not just code.
verification: Installed-package two-clone close/commit/merge/pull; stale/missing projection; detail/list/planning agreement; conflicts and resolved retry; identity/history/context preservation.

title: Bounded external issue ingestion
requirement: Explicit GitHub ingestion shall use gh extraction and an Application-owned validated write plan with source provenance, identity matching, preview, idempotence and recovery.
rationale: Complete repeatable import supports dogfooding without two writable authorities.
verification: Selected/missing/invalid records; paginated comments/timeline; original attribution; existing legacy mapping; unchanged retry; changed source revisions; preserved local fields; concurrent edits; partial extraction and interrupted writes; no credential persistence or network on ordinary core reads.

title: External closure delivery correctness
requirement: GitHub-only closure shall become an attributable canonical repository change through an explicitly defined acquisition and commit path before the promised pull can expose local completion.
rationale: A remote tracker mutation is not itself a Git repository change.
verification: Review ownership/timing and conflicting/reopened-state policy; prove two-clone delivery, source identity, idempotent retry, failed acquisition/commit visibility, preserved local context and separation from requirement verification.

title: Committed outbound GitHub closure publication
requirement: Application shall plan closures from an immutable Git snapshot through a narrow source port and publish through an independent gh adapter, wired by Bootstrap and invoked by explicit CLI or default-branch Action.
rationale: One-way publication supports dogfooding while preserving Git authority and independent adapters.
verification: Test uncommitted exclusion; committed reopen exclusion; offline preview; malformed/duplicate targets; exact remote identity and PR rejection; pagination; evidence-post/close interruption and retry; bounded failures; no local receipts; workflow permissions/concurrency and live post-merge proof.
